entries.explanation_en: After a time expression, 에 says when something happens.
Marks the noun that is the subject of a statement.
Sets up the noun that the rest of the statement is about; it can also signal contrast.
Connects a noun to another noun it owns or is related to.
Marks the noun affected by the verb.
Follows a name before a noun to say what that person or thing is called.
Marks the name or words used with a verb such as ‘call’ or ‘say’.
Places the action or state before now. The written form changes with the preceding stem.
Ends a statement in a formal, polite style.
Turns a descriptive word into a modifier placed before its noun.
After an action verb, this form describes a noun by an action already completed.
Forms a modifier for an action considered possible or expected; before 수 it helps express ability or possibility.
Connects a noun to what someone or something is. It can take past and polite endings.
A verb in its -(으)ㄹ modifier form followed by 수 없다 means that doing it is not possible.
